title: Plug-in closing: forced Disk Map unload in a shell command, stray comparator box
problem: Two leftovers of the plug-in window closing work. (1) Disk Map (143): a forced unload (the core's "force?" answered Yes) while a shell command of the map is running (a command of its context menu, a shell confirmation) terminates the map's thread inside the shell (`KillAll(TRUE)`), as in every release; the Debug build then shows its leak reports (monitored handles, CRT). (2) File Comparator, hex view (147 review LOW-2): its `WM_DESTROY` pump (`PM_REMOVE`) can dispatch a pending `WM_USER_HANDLEFILEERROR` and show a stray error box while the window closes; no crash path, reachability low (posted messages come before paint; the window is hidden first). Next to it, a trap for later work: `CFileMapping::Destroy` does not reset `FileSize`, so a later paint would post "handle is invalid".
evidence: Migrated from specs/NEXT-WORK.md §A item 1 (L124) and item 3 (L151) (at 7993914c). Disk Map: specs/143-diskmap-release-guard/fix-log.md, *Work* (probe row E5: "the forced unload terminates the map's thread inside the shell (`KillAll(TRUE)`, every release) and the Debug build shows its leak reports"); probe in specs/143-diskmap-release-guard/probe/ (rows E4, E5). File Comparator: specs/147-plugin-close-boxes/fix-log.md, *Review*, LOW-2 (`filecomp` hex view `WM_DESTROY`, `CFileMapping::Destroy`).
expected: A forced unload during a Disk Map shell command does not terminate a thread inside the shell (it waits for the shell call to return, or is declined with a message); the comparator's hex view shows no error box once its close began; `CFileMapping::Destroy` resets `FileSize`.
approach: Measure first: 143's probe row E5 drives the forced unload. Terminating the thread is the core's "force" semantics (147's review calls the comparable LOW-3 exactly that), so keeping it is a valid outcome for part (1).
notes: Low: part (1) needs the user to force the unload, part (2) a narrow timing. If the forced termination is accepted as the force semantics, park or reject part (1) with that reason and keep part (2).
log: feature 143 done; the forced unload during a shell command recorded as left
feature 147 done; its review recorded the hex view's stray box (LOW-2)

title: Viewer Copy to File onto a file held open, on a FAT stick or a network share
problem: Feature 173 made the viewer's Copy to File replace an existing file in one step (`SalReplaceWithTempW`) instead of delete-then-move. The loss it guards against is not producible on Windows 11 NTFS (POSIX delete semantics); the classic semantics - the name stays until the last handle closes - are those of FAT / exFAT and SMB shares, and none was available to the probe (`\\localhost\C$` refused, no FAT volume). The "kept in the temporary file" message was not driven either.
evidence: Migrated from specs/NEXT-WORK.md §A item 5c (L176) (at 7993914c). specs/173-viewer-copy-replace/fix-log.md (rows HELD and LOCKED; "Not driven: the 'kept in the temporary file' message").
expected: The target keeps its old content or gets the new one - it never disappears; a kept temporary file is named in a message.
steps: On a FAT or exFAT USB stick: in the viewer, Copy to File onto an existing file that another program holds open - the target keeps its old content or gets the new one, never disappears
The same on a network share (SMB)
If a message names a kept temporary file: the file exists and holds the new content

problem: Feature 153 marks, in the Archive Update dialog, a file whose member changed in the archive since its F4. Recorded limits: (1) an archive or member rewritten with the same size and time is not told apart (FAT 2 s times, `7z -stl`) - the warning is missing; (2) a daylight-saving / time-zone change between the F4 and the update can mark a member needlessly (the ZIP plug-in converts DOS times with the current offset); (3) a changed archive is listed twice on the refresh path (once by the check, once by the reopen) - a cost on large archives.

title: A file moved aside to salNNN can stay there silently on the create paths
problem: When a rename, a move or a create hits another entry's 8.3 short name, that entry is moved aside to `salNNN`, the operation done, and the entry moved back. Feature 221 retries a failed move-back and reports it for Quick Rename and the worker's move. Left: (1) the create paths `SalCreateFileEx`, `SalCreateDirectoryEx` and `SafeFileCreate` have no window - a failed move-back is still only a trace, so the user's file stays renamed to `salNNN` and nothing says so (an out parameter would be needed); (2) PictView's and the Renamer's move-back report the failure but have no retry (`SalMoveFile` through the plug-in interface - a local loop each).
evidence: Migrated from specs/NEXT-WORK.md §A item 11 (L297) (at 7993914c). specs/221-moved-aside-restore/fix-log.md (lines ~36-40, "Recorded in specs/NEXT-WORK.md"); the earlier chain: features 199, 201, 202, 203.
expected: On every route a failed move-back is retried and, if it still fails, the user is told which entry was left under which `salNNN` name.
approach: Not drivable as it stands: the failure is a race (another process holds the entry between the two moves); 221's approach - a seam or a held handle in the probe - applies.
notes: Severity: the content is never lost, it is left under another name; narrow (a scanner or an indexer holding the entry at that moment).

title: Renamer: regular expressions judge \b, \w, classes and '.' by single bytes
problem: The Renamer's regular-expression engine still judges `\b`, `\w`, `\d`, `\s`, POSIX classes, '.', bracket classes and a quantifier after a multi-byte letter by single bytes: a pattern that would split a UTF-8 letter is refused "(123)"; a `\xC5\xBD` escape matches neither case when case-insensitive (it matched the capital before 210); bracket ranges with non-ASCII bounds are meaningless over UTF-8; letters outside the BMP and combining marks break words; the Greek final sigma does not fold with sigma (a match missed, never a wrong letter). expected: Classes, '.', `\b` and quantifiers work on whole UTF-8 letters; no pattern is refused for splitting a letter; the history and the preview sort compare by the file system's rule or by whole letters.
